newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's EDENOR gets $120 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's EDENOR gets $120 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Argentine electricity distributor EDENOR SA said Monday the Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) arranged a syndicated $120 million loan it will channel to investment plans.

The loan comprises two tranches, one of $40 million granted by the IADB with a 2.75 percent interest spread over LIBOR and maturity March 31, 2005, and another of $80 million granted by a syndicate of banks, over seven years with a 2.0 percent spread over LIBOR, EDENOR said in a press release.
Both tranches carry a two year grace period and disimbursement is scheduled for April.

Fifty-one percent of EDENOR is held by Electricidad Argentina SA EASA, formed by Electricite de France, Spain's Enher, and Argentine oil company ASTRA, with 25 percent each, and Spain's Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA (ENDESA), France's Saur and J.P. Morgan Co Inc with 8.33 percent each.

Ten percent is held by employees and the remaining 39 percent is in the hands of Electricite de France (7.33 percent), Credit Lyonnais (9.77), Saur (2.44), Spain's Banco Santander SA (9.72) and ENDESA's unit ENDESAR (9.74).
